bull.t: Low leverage and improved equity position
bull.b: Very low debt reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while Immunic advances its clinical programs. The return to positive, sizable TTM equity also represents a material capital-structure improvement, although continued losses could erode this support over time.

bull.t: Multiple sclerosis pipeline nearing pivotal milestones
bull.b: The lead multiple sclerosis program is advancing toward consequential late-stage development milestones, which could clarify its regulatory and commercial potential. Progress across relapsing and progressive MS also gives the pipeline a focused opportunity to build value from one therapeutic franchise.

bull.t: Stronger biopharma finance and capital-markets oversight
bull.b: Adding an experienced biopharma finance and capital-markets leader can improve strategic oversight as Immunic approaches clinical, regulatory and financing decisions. Her background may strengthen board-level evaluation of funding options and commercialization planning during the company’s next development phase.

bear.t: No revenue and persistent large losses
bear.b: Immunic remains pre-commercial, so it has no product revenue to offset research and development costs. Persistent losses of this scale reduce internal funding capacity and leave future financial progress dependent on successful development, commercialization or additional external capital.

bear.t: High cash burn and financing dependence
bear.b: Substantial ongoing cash consumption means Immunic is not yet self-funding and will likely require financing while clinical programs continue. This constrains capital-allocation flexibility and makes the company more exposed to dilution or funding pressure if development timelines extend.

The investment case remains highly dependent on clinical results and regulatory progress for vidofludimus calcium. Trial setbacks, regulatory challenges, intellectual-property issues or financing constraints could delay development and materially reduce the pipeline’s eventual commercial opportunity.
